content.summary_of_the_paper:
In this paper, the authors concentrate on the image-level weakly-supervised instance segmentation task by proposing a compositional image augmentation pipeline named Exact. In particular, the designed module comprises three components: foreground extraction, background segmentation, and compositional paste. 

In the foreground extraction module, the authors utilize Entity Segmentation and Grad-CAM to generate inputs for the F-EM algorithm so as to extract foreground objects. Next, a training set image is fed into the Image Captioning module and the generated description is used to synthesize images via the text-to-image synthesis DALL-E model. Finally, foreground objects are pasted into both original images and generated images to create a synthetic dataset with pseudo instance labels.

The main contribution of this work is proposing a compositional augmentation framework for weakly instance segmentation tasks, especially in the foreground extraction component. It leverages knowledge of pre-trainings through Grad-CAM and matches predicted masks from a certain pre-trained instance segmentation model. 

Experiments show the effectiveness of the Exact augmentation framework on benchmarks and exceed state-of-the-art methods with large margins.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
The pipeline flow as well as the most crucial component module, foreground extraction, were well discussed by the authors. This paper is organized and well-presented. 

The idea of using Grad-CAM as reliable guidance for extracting binary masks via an EM-based algorithm is comparatively fascinating. 

The performance of the proposed Exact framework in image-level weakly instance segmentation is sufficiently validated. Moreover, the authors evaluate the performance on long-tail conditions and object detection tasks as well. 

Weaknesses:
Although this work outperforms cutting-edge approaches, the proposed pipeline consists of several outstanding components and it is not fair when compared to others. For example, the authors leverage DALL-E for text-to-image synthesis and CLIP for background selection,...

More importantly, this work is a combination of many off-the-shelf methods and the contribution is not much impressive and essential as well. To be specific, this pipeline comprises Entity Segmentation, Grad-CAM, EM-based algorithm, image captioning, DALL-E, CLIP, and Copy-Paste augmentation, …

Furthermore, some main components in this work apply available ideas which do not persuade me that this paper should be considered a significant novelty. The augmentation method of creating virtual backgrounds and then pasting objects on them for instance segmentation tasks is common. In addition, take the example of the F-EM algorithm, the idea of applying EM for image segmentation tasks is not very rare. 

The designed framework contains several modules but lacks experiments in replacing certain ones with other SOTA methods to assess the contribution of each module. I suggest that DALL-E should be replaced by Imagen, Stable Diffusion,...
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
This paper coherently describes each component and performs experiments comprehensively to illustrate the improvement of the Exact. The ablation study provides adequate information for choosing hyperparameters in this framework. 

However, as I mentioned above, this work is a combination of available modules and some key ideas are borrowed from the existing works. Moreover, the way of combining everything can increase the computational costs significantly, which is not evaluated in this work.
content.summary_of_the_review: The main contribution of this work is proposing a compositional augmentation strategy for image-level instance segmentation tasks. This pipeline consists of several heavy modules (DALL-E, CLIP,...), and the ideas learn from off-the-shelf methods (EM for segmentation, Copy-Paste,...). Experiments also lack replacement of contained module with a variety of options to assess the contribution of each one.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a compositional image augmentation pipeline for weakly-supervised instance segmentation using only image-level supervision. The proposed method consists of three main components. 1) An EMlike approach is proposed to iteratively refine an initial set of object proposals generated by a generic entity segmentation method, thereby generating high-quality foreground object masks. 2) High-quality context-aware background images are generated using a text-to-image compositional synthesis method like DALL·E. 3) A large-scale pseudo-labeled instance segmentation training dataset is presented by compositing the foreground object masks onto the original and generated background images. The proposed approach achieves state-of-the-art weakly-supervised instance segmentation results on both the PASCAL VOC 2012 and MS COCO dataset by using only image-level, weak label information.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
1) This method outperforms the best baseline by +7.4 and +2.8 mAP0.50 on PASCAL and COCO, respectively.
2) This method provides a new solution to the long-tail weakly-supervised instance segmentation problem (when many classes may only have few training samples), by selectively augmenting under-represented classes.

Weaknesses:
1) The three steps in the EXACT method are generally lacking in motivation as to how the authors came up with the idea to design the method in this way. My point is that EXACT seems to achieve good results technically, but the contribution here is limited to the technical side and does not help the community as a whole too much in terms of understanding the problem.

2) The authors do not show an ablation experiment of the EXACT method on COCO. As in Table 2, though EXACT achieves a SOTA result, this result is somewhat unconvincing. I'm curious how much performance improvement is brought by DALL-E in the current results? 
In addition, I have some concerns on the fairness of the results in the long tail section. Is DALL-E used to assist in this section?  If yes, it is indeed equivalent to introducing more external knowledge. 

3) I have also some concerns on the fairness of the results in Table 4, due to the inconsistency of the backbone networks.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Overall, this paper is well wrtten, and the proposed method is easy to follow. However, since the motivation of the proposed steps is not well presented, it affects my evaluation of the novelty of this paper.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a copy-paste compositional image augmentation pipeline based weak-supervision for boosting instance segmentation. They first obtain foreground masks based on a trained classifier with the activation map region, and remove the outlier proposals with EM. For background images, then they use DALL-E to generate them. Later, copy-paste operation is implemented to augment synthetic composite images. The results have shown improved performance on instance segmentation.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Pros:
+) The paper shows potential of copy-paste object patch based image composition can boost instance segmentation.
+) The paper extensively studies experiments compared with SOTA methods.

Cons:
-) Novely seems limited. Copy-paste has been proved effective for semantic segmentation in previous methods. 
-) The paper shows a more engineering perspective without clear technical contribution. It is a fact that with more object patches in the training data with given/preprocessed labels, the performance of instance segmentation will get improved. 
-) Since new information is introduced (using pretrained DALL-E), it is not clear which parts promotes the performance (background image vs. inserted object patch). More ablation study should be implemented, e.g. compose object patches into training dataset. 
-) Lack of comparison of computation cost.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
-) The paper lacks of novelty. 
+) The paper is written well and clear.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper designs a copy-paste based image composition method for boosting instance segmentation. The paper lacks of novelty with limited technical contribution in terms of method design. Besides, experimental setup is flawed, which makes it hard to validate the proposed method.

content.title: EXACT: Compositional Augmentation for Image-level Weakly-Supervised Instance Segmentation
content.abstract: We propose EXACT: EXtract-AugContext-pasTe, a compositional image augmentation pipeline for weakly-supervised instance segmentation using only image-level supervision. The proposed method consists of three main components. The first component generates high-quality foreground object masks. To this end, an EM-like approach is proposed that iteratively refines an initial set of object mask proposals generated by a generic entity segmentation method. Next, in the second component, high-quality context-aware background images are generated using a text-to-image compositional synthesis method like DALL-E. Finally, the third component creates a large-scale pseudo-labeled instance segmentation training dataset by compositing the foreground object masks onto the original and generated background images. The proposed approach achieves state-of-the-art weakly-supervised instance segmentation results on both the PASCAL VOC 2012 and MS COCO dataset by using only image-level, weak label information. In particular, it outperforms the best baseline by +7.4 and +2.8 mAP-0.50 on PASCAL and COCO, respectively. Further, the method provides a new solution to the long-tail weakly-supervised instance segmentation problem (when many classes may only have few training samples), by selectively augmenting under-represented classes.
